court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Smt. Asha Raghu Roman vs Mumbai Board Of Trustees Of The Port Of ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Smt. Asha Raghu Roman, widow and wife
parties.respondent_defendant: Mumbai Board of Trustees of the Port of Mumbai, a Statutory Corporation and Finance Department, Pension Branch, Mumbai Port Trust

facts_of_case: Petitioner is the widow of one Raghu Sakhru Roman. She claims she was married to another gentleman Shri Zimesh Darshrath Phapale but they separated and executed a Deed of Divorce. She then married the deceased Raghu on 21-9-2010.

legal_principles.principle: A decree of dissolution of marriage by mutual consent is effective from the date of execution of the deed, not from the date claimed by the parties.
legal_principles.held: Since the respondents insisted on a Court's order, the petitioner along with her ex-husband Zimesh Phapale filed Marriage Petition No.373 of 2014 in the Court of Civil Judge, Senior Division at Khed, District Pune.

legal_principles.principle: A court's decree is binding on all parties, including the respondents.
legal_principles.held: After obtaining that declaration and the correction, as aforesaid, the petitioner approached respondent No.2-Finance Department which issued a communication dated 31-3-2016.

outcome.final_order: The writ petition is taken up for hearing and final disposal.
